title: Plainly: the inbox is a file, I do not watch it, and the real delay is 12 to 30 seconds

text:
Yes, the inbox is a log file the assistant appends to. I do not watch it and I do not poll it. It is only the written record.
What actually wakes me is the doorbell: the assistant sends a message straight to my session. If I am idle, that message wakes me at once, no waiting for a timer or a skill. If I am in the middle of a step, I see it when that step ends.
The real delay, measured from the six relays so far, from the moment your words hit the inbox to my answer on your screen: 12, 13, 19, 26 and 30 seconds, and about a minute for the first hello. Almost all of that is me reading, thinking and writing; the delivery itself takes about a second.
What would make it instant: nothing makes me instant, because every answer of mine is a full turn of a large model. The instant layer is the assistant, and its answers will start appearing word by word within a second or two once the streaming pipe lands. The right shape is: the assistant answers you at once, I do the work and update the cards.
